delete.description: Delete an image: its files first, then the record.

get.description:
The image as a file the browser saves (browsers ignore `download` on links to the
storage host, ADR-0034).

post.description:
Copy the image into the person's export folder (the desktop app sets one; a webview
cannot save a file by itself). Never overwrites: a second copy gets a number.

delete.description:
Delete a clip (or dismiss a failed one): its files first, then the record. A clip still
being made cannot be deleted: its job is running.

get.description:
The clip as a file the browser saves (browsers ignore `download` on links to the
storage host, ADR-0034).

A file the browser saves. Browsers ignore `download` on links to another origin (the
storage host), so files are served from here with a Content-Disposition. The song is looked
up for this user only, like every other route.

`audio` is the MP3 with the title, lyrics and cover art written into its tag, so a music
player shows the cover. `video` is the cover as a picture with the song playing, made on the
first request and kept in storage.
The languages to choose from, and what an upload may be.

delete.description: Delete a transcript (or dismiss a failed one). One still being made cannot be deleted.

get.description: The transcript as a file the browser saves: plain text, SRT, WebVTT or JSON.

delete.description: Delete a result: its file first, then the record.

get.description:
The speech as a file the browser saves (browsers ignore `download` on links to the
storage host, ADR-0034).
The languages and voices the form offers: a gender with no voice is an empty list.

delete.description:
Delete a clip (or dismiss a failed one): its files first, then the record. A clip still
being made cannot be deleted: its job is running.

get.description:
The clip as a file the browser saves (browsers ignore `download` on links to the
storage host, ADR-0034).

delete.description: Remove the caller's own unused upload (the user took the file back, ADR-0039).

post.description:
A recording or a video file (ADR-0043): checked by its first bytes, decoded to a clean
16 kHz mono WAV (no video, no tags) in a limited child process, and stored in its place.
